subject.title: fix(memory-core): skip unchanged Dreaming workspace state writes

question: Should Memory Core prioritize zero unchanged workspace-state writes, accepting that unchanged rows no longer refresh created_at and can be evicted first at the 50,000-row cap?
rationale: The change is intentional and well-tested, but it modifies the retention semantics of existing persisted workspace state under capacity pressure; tests can demonstrate either policy but cannot choose the product contract.

options.title: Accept no-op-write priority
options.body: Approve the documented policy that stable equal rows do not refresh recency, preserving the gateway-stall reduction and its focused eviction test.

options.title: Preserve refresh-based retention
options.body: Require an owner-approved design that preserves current created_at refresh semantics while avoiding the broad rewrite cost.

options.title: Pause the optimization
options.body: Keep the current behavior until Memory Core has a clear capacity-retention contract and migration or compatibility story.

recommendation.title: Accept no-op-write priority
recommendation.body: Approve the documented policy that stable equal rows do not refresh recency, preserving the gateway-stall reduction and its focused eviction test.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the implementation, direct keyed-store contract analysis, and the focused capacity regression that frame the decision.
